from scim2_filter_parser.attr_paths import AttrPath as AttrPathWrapper
from scim2_filter_parser.transpilers.sql import AttrPath, Transpiler

attr_map = {
    ('emails', 'type', None): 'emails.type',
    ('emails', 'value', None): 'emails.value',
    ('userName', None, None): 'username',
}

# Named access on first_path / iteration
q = AttrPathWrapper('emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"', attr_map)
first = q.first_path

EOF

import json
from scim2_filter_parser.attr_paths import AttrPath as AttrPathWrapper
from scim2_filter_parser.transpilers.sql import AttrPath, Transpiler

attr_map = {
    ('emails', 'type', None): 'emails.type',
    ('emails', 'value', None): 'emails.value',
    ('userName', None, None): 'username',
}

# 1) Named access on first_path / iteration
q = AttrPathWrapper('emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"', attr_map)
first = q.first_path
print("first_path:", first)
print("first_path.attr_name:", first.attr_name)
print("first_path.sub_attr:", first.sub_attr)
print("first_path.uri:", first.uri)
for p in q:
    assert (p.attr_name, p.sub_attr, p.uri) == tuple(p), "named vs index mismatch"
    print("path:", p.attr_name, p.sub_attr, p.uri)

# 2) Backward compat: equality with plain tuple
assert first == ('emails', 'type', None)

# 3) Hashable + usable as dict key alongside plain-tuple keys in attr_map
assert hash(first) == hash(('emails', 'type', None))
assert attr_map[AttrPath('userName', None, None)] == 'username'
assert Transpiler(attr_map).attr_map.get(AttrPath('userName', None, None)) == 'username'

# 4) json serialization (str(AttrPath) -> json.dumps of list) still works
assert json.loads(str(q)) == [["emails", "type", None], ["emails", "value", None]], str(q)

# 5) It's still a tuple subclass
assert isinstance(first, tuple) and isinstance(first, AttrPath)

print("ALL CHECKS PASSED")
EOF
